problems.title: Two Sum
problems.quickshot: PATTERN: complement lookup. If you must find a pair that hits a target, don't recheck pairs — remember what you've seen in a Map so the partner is one lookup away.
problems.dsExplainer: HashMap: a dictionary from key→value with average O(1) insert and lookup. Here we map each number's VALUE to its INDEX so we can instantly ask 'did I already see target - x?'.

approaches.name: Brute Force
approaches.idea: Test every pair until one adds up to the target.
steps: Fix the first number, then try every number to its right as the partner.
Starting j at i + 1 avoids reusing an element and avoids repeating pairs.

approaches.name: Hash Map
approaches.idea: Walk once, remembering every number you have already passed.
steps: For the current number, the partner it needs is exactly target − nums[i].
Keep a map from value to index for every number already visited.

problems.title: Two Sum II
problems.quickshot: PATTERN: two pointers on sorted data. Sorted + pair-target ⇒ converge from both ends; the sort tells you which pointer to move.
problems.dsExplainer: Two pointers: two indices (l, r) walking a sorted array. Moving l up increases the sum; moving r down decreases it — so you steer straight to the target.

approaches.name: Two Pointers
approaches.idea: Sum the two ends; too big → move right in, too small → move left in.
steps: The array is sorted, so the ends give the extreme sums.
Each step eliminates one impossible pairing.

frames.what: Sum of ends = 17. Too big → move right in.
frames.why: Because the array is sorted, moving the correct pointer always steps toward the answer.

Longest Substring Without Repeating
problems.quickshot: PATTERN: variable sliding window. 'Longest/shortest contiguous run with a rule' ⇒ grow the right edge, shrink the left when the rule breaks.
problems.dsExplainer: Sliding window + HashSet: the set holds the characters currently inside the window so duplicates are detected in O(1). The window [l..r] expands and contracts.

approaches.name: Sliding Window
approaches.idea: Expand the window to the right; on a duplicate, shrink from the left until it's unique again.
steps: The set is the window's memory of which chars are inside.
Each index enters and leaves the window at most once → linear.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.quickshot: PATTERN: binary search. Sorted + a yes/no that flips once ⇒ halve the range each step.
problems.dsExplainer: Binary search maintains an invariant window [lo, hi] that always contains the answer if it exists, shrinking it by half each probe → O(log n).

approaches.name: Binary Search
approaches.idea: Look at the middle, then keep only the half that can contain the target.
steps: Compare the midpoint to the target.
Discard the half that cannot possibly hold the answer.

problems.quickshot: PATTERN: Kadane / running optimum. Max contiguous sum ⇒ carry a running sum; drop it the moment it turns negative.
problems.dsExplainer: Dynamic programming in O(1) space: 'best sum ending here' only depends on the previous 'best ending here', so two variables suffice.

approaches.name: Kadane's Algorithm
approaches.idea: At each element, either extend the current run or restart from this element.
steps: A negative running sum can only hurt what comes next.
Track the best sum seen anywhere along the way.
